## Costs, evidence and deadline consequences

For the immediate #11 delivery, the historical serial path after readiness is
50 minutes of upstream gates, 15 minutes publication work, 35 minutes consumer
pin/wiring, and 3 hours consumer CI: **4 hours 40 minutes**. These are observed
historical costs, not a forecast or upper bound. #11's independent implementation
review is already complete, but queueing, release preparation, any needed
correction/review, registry delays and failed runs remain unknown. Three parallel
native platforms remain required; their runner consumption must not be added as
if it were wall-clock time. The historical combined CI workload per cycle is
**11.5 runner-hours**.

This plan accepts a second release/adoption cycle to meet the earlier useful
outcome. Two historical-sized cycles would total 9 hours 20 minutes of serial
stage work and 23 runner-hours across both deliveries, excluding the redesign
and other unknowns. Those totals are aggregate work illustrations, not the
critical path of the first release or a prediction for either future run. A
three-week #12 estimate dominates any two-day deadline argument for batching;
there is no justified numerical speedup claim.
